Good news — Russian citizens can currently visit Vietnam visa-free.

1. **Primary pathway: Visa-free entry.** Russians are on Vietnam's unilateral visa exemption list, so no visa is needed for a standard visit.
2. **Key details:** You can stay up to **45 days** per visit under this exemption. It's currently valid **until 2028-03-05** (extended per a March 2025 announcement) — worth double-checking it hasn't changed by the time you travel. Your passport also needs at least 180 days of validity remaining from your entry date.
3. **E-Visa as a fallback:** If you need to stay longer than 45 days (or want a multiple-entry option), an e-Visa is available to all nationalities, including Russians — up to 90 days, costing USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), with 2-3 business day processing via evisa.gov.vn.
4. **Data caveat:** This is based on data as of 2026-08-17. Immigration policy can change, so it's a good idea to verify the current rules at https://evisa.gov.vn/ before you travel.

As a Filipino traveler, you'll need an e-Visa for a 30-day stay in Vietnam — Philippine passport holders only get visa-free entry for up to 21 days, and your trip is longer than that.

1. **Apply for an e-Visa** at the official portal: https://evisa.gov.vn/
2. **Cost:** USD 25 for a single-entry e-Visa, or USD 50 for multiple-entry.
3. **Stay length:** The e-Visa covers up to 90 days, so your 30-day trip is comfortably within the limit.
4. **Processing time:** Typically 2-3 business days (faster/expedited options are available for an extra fee).
5. **Entry:** The e-Visa is valid for entry by air, land, or sea at any approved port (83 ports currently listed) — you're not locked into one specific entry point.
6. **Passport validity:** Make sure your passport is valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.

Note: If you were staying 21 days or fewer, you could enter visa-free under the Philippines-Vietnam bilateral agreement — but since you're planning 30 days, the e-Visa is the correct route.

This is based on policy data as of 2026-08-17. Visa rules can change, so it's worth double-checking current requirements at evisa.gov.vn before you book your trip.

As a Belarusian citizen, Vietnam and Belarus have a mutual visa-exemption agreement (in effect since 30 Jan 2025): up to 30 days visa-free per entry, but your total stay cannot exceed 90 days within a calendar year. You've already used 70 of those 90 days this year, so adding 30 more days under the visa-free exemption would put you at 100 days total — 10 days over the annual cap. That means you cannot cover this next stretch of the trip on the visa exemption alone.

Your practical option: apply for an e-Visa instead. It's open to all nationalities (since 15 Aug 2023), allows stays of up to 90 days, and costs USD 25 for single-entry or USD 50 for multiple-entry, with 2-3 business day processing at evisa.gov.vn (expedited options exist for a higher fee). Nothing in the current data ties the e-Visa to the same 90-day/calendar-year limit that applies to the bilateral exemption, so it should let you add the extra 30 days — but because you're right at the edge of the exemption's annual cap, double-check with evisa.gov.vn or a Vietnamese consulate before you travel to confirm border officials will treat the two entry types independently.

One more requirement either way: your passport must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.

This is based on policy data as of 2026-08-17 — please verify current rules at https://evisa.gov.vn/ before finalizing your plans.

As an Indian passport holder, you do not have visa-free access to Vietnam — India is not on Vietnam's visa-exemption list, so a visa is required regardless of trip length.

So the recommended route is an embassy/consulate visa: apply at a Vietnamese embassy or consulate in the appropriate category (e.g. an LV visa if it's a longer-stay visit visa, DT for investment, or GD for education/study), since only that route can be issued for a period beyond 90 days.

For reference, the e-Visa option (available to all nationalities, including India) covers stays up to 90 days, costs USD 25 for a single entry or USD 50 for multiple entries, is processed in about 2-3 business days (faster options exist for a fee), and can be used at any of the approved air/land/sea ports — apply at evisa.gov.vn. It just isn't long enough on its own for a 4-month stay.

A couple of other notes: your passport must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date, and this data is current as of 2026-08-17 — I'd recommend confirming the latest requirements and exact visa category directly with your nearest Vietnamese embassy/consulate or at evisa.gov.vn before you apply.

Yes — Americans can visit Phu Quoc Island without a visa.

Vietnam's Phu Quoc exemption is open to all nationalities, including U.S. citizens, and lets you enter with no visa at all as long as you arrive directly from outside Vietnam (by air or sea) and stay only on the island.

Key details:
- Stay length: up to 30 days visa-free
- Restriction: you must stay on Phu Quoc Island — traveling to mainland Vietnam voids the exemption and would require a separate visa
- Entry modes allowed: air or sea only
- Passport validity: must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date

If you want to visit mainland Vietnam too (not just Phu Quoc), you'd need a regular e-Visa instead — that option is available to all nationalities, allows stays up to 90 days, and costs USD 25 (single-entry) to USD 50 (multiple-entry), applied for at evisa.gov.vn (processing is typically 2-3 business days).

This data is current as of 2026-08-17 — I'd recommend double-checking at evisa.gov.vn before you travel in case policy has changed.
